universities.name: Indian Institute of Technology Madras
universities.summary: Indian Institute of Technology Madras is a public institute in Chennai offering engineering, science, humanities, management and research degrees. Its residential campus supports laboratory and project-based study, while separate non-campus and international interdisciplinary programmes have their own admission and delivery arrangements.
universities.campusLifestyle: The wooded Chennai campus brings together academic buildings, laboratories, hostels, sports and student clubs. Gajendra Circle connects the residential, academic and hostel zones. Campus activities include technical and cultural events, student organisations and innovation projects. Non-campus BS learners study through their separate online and examination arrangements rather than receiving a residential campus place.
universities.cityProfile: The Chennai campus entrance is on Sardar Patel Road, near Adyar and Velachery, with the address IIT Madras, Chennai 600036. Internal buses connect the gate, Gajendra Circle, academic areas and hostel zones. The campus is distinct from IIT Madras Zanzibar in Tanzania and from partner institutions used by joint programmes. Check the exact reporting or examination location on the offer, particularly for non-campus degrees and joint or field-deployment routes.
universities.practicalExposure: Residential engineering master’s programmes combine core and elective courses with project work; approved projects may involve industry or other organisations. Science and engineering curricula include discipline-specific laboratory and computational study. The MBA combines cases, management internship and project work. International interdisciplinary M.Tech programmes add cross-department coursework and a thesis. Cybersecurity includes two years of field deployment after its campus coursework. Electronic Systems and Aeronautics non-campus degrees require specified practical visits; these arrangements differ from full-time campus study.
universities.hostelOverview: First-year residential undergraduates normally share rooms; later single, double or triple allocations depend on the hostel. Postgraduates use shared or single rooms. Wardens, resident assistant wardens and hostel councils support administration. Hostel and advance mess charges are separate from tuition and require the current notice. Non-campus BS enrolment does not guarantee a hostel place for examinations or laboratory visits; accompanying parents must arrange their own stay.
universities.dietarySupport: Residential dining includes North Indian and South Indian vegetarian and non-vegetarian choices, with institute dining facilities and campus eateries. Mess selection, meal costs and any special dietary requirement should be confirmed before joining. Online learners attending practical sessions need separate accommodation and meal arrangements.
universities.safetyOverview: Institute identity cards and regulated visitor passes form part of campus access requirements. The campus hospital provides general care, visiting specialists and ambulance facilities. Students should obtain the current emergency and reporting contacts when joining; these services do not establish a guaranteed response time.
universities.studentSupport: Faculty academic advice, hostel wardens and student administration support residential study. The Office of Global Engagement guides international admissions and arrival formalities, with separate insurance requirements. The campus hospital supports healthcare needs; non-campus learners use their programme’s registration and course-support channels.
whyChoose: Discipline-specific engineering, science, humanities and management study with laboratory or project components.
A residential campus with academic, hostel, student-activity and healthcare facilities.
Distinct international interdisciplinary and non-campus pathways with documented degree and admission requirements.
thingsToConsider: JoSAA, IAT, GATE, JAM, CAT/GMAT, Cybersecurity and non-campus qualifier routes have different qualification and nationality rules.
Tuition varies sharply by Indian, foreign, ICCR and sponsored categories; hostel, mess, deposits and other charges are separate.
A non-campus degree, a partner programme or a field-deployment route has different location and accommodation arrangements from residential study.
bestFitFor: Applicants who can meet the exact examination, qualifying-subject and nationality rules for their chosen route.
Students interested in engineering/science analysis, laboratory work, research-oriented projects or advanced disciplinary study.
Learners who have checked whether the programme is residential, international interdisciplinary, joint, non-campus or a professional route.

faq.question: Which undergraduate admission route applies?
faq.answer: Most residential BTech and named BS or direct dual degrees use JEE Advanced and JoSAA. BS Medical Sciences and Engineering and BS Chemistry instead use IAT with separate IIT Madras allocation. Bachelor of Cybersecurity uses the documented joint IIT Kanpur selection process. These routes cannot be substituted for each other.

faq.question: Are current science degrees four-year BS or older BS/MS awards?
faq.answer: The 2026 joining schedule identifies four-year BS in Biological Science, Physics, Mathematics, Chemistry and Medical Sciences and Engineering. Older central descriptions of BS/MS dual degrees should not be treated as another current admission offer. Any later upgrade or exit option has its own conditions.

faq.question: What are the IAT-route qualification and nationality limits?
faq.answer: For 2026, applicants need IAT qualification and Class XII science in 2024, 2025 or 2026, with 60% aggregate or 55% for SC/ST/PwD. Medical Sciences and Engineering requires Mathematics plus two of Biology/Chemistry/Physics; Chemistry requires Chemistry plus two of Biology/Mathematics/Physics. Only Indian nationals or the specified pre 4 March 2021 OCI/PIO cardholders are eligible.

faq.question: How does Bachelor of Cybersecurity differ from a BTech?
faq.answer: The dedicated four-year B.Cyber. has two years of IIT Madras coursework followed by two years of field deployment in selected government organisations. Its 2026 route is Indian-national only and uses JEE Main 2025/26 performance, prior cybersecurity work and the joint test/hackathon process. IIT Kanpur fees are not an IIT Madras fee quote.

faq.question: What determines MTech eligibility?
faq.answer: The programme’s accepted qualifying subject and GATE paper must both match. Regular 2026 entry accepts the stated GATE 2024/25/26 scores; eligible IIT B.Tech. graduates with CGPA 8/10 orabove can use departmental review without GATE. HTTA/non-HTTA are funding categories, not different degree awards. Sponsored and international routes have separate requirements.

faq.question: Do MA and MSc use the same entrance process?
faq.answer: No. Regular MA uses programme-specific GATEX Hpapers and accepts qualifying undergraduate disciplines. Regular MSc uses JAM and the exact subject-duration requirements for Chemistry, Mathematics or Physics. International admission assesses degree relevance and language/grade requirements separately; domestic subject conditions are not automatically the overseas route.

faq.question: Which joining dates are verified?
faq.answer: The 2026 residential undergraduate cohort began classes 30 July 2026, and postgraduate classes began 27 July 2026. Future cohorts need their own joining notices. The non-campus BS portals currently name a January 2027 qualifier/admission term with 29 January 2027 applicationdeadline; that is not a promise of regular foundation classes on 1 January.

faq.question: What tuition applies to Indian applicants?
faq.answer: For the 2026–27 entry schedule, semester tuition is INR 100,000 for UG, INR 25,000 for MTech/MSc, INR 20,000 for MA and INR 250,000 for MBA, before applicable remissions. Annual baselines multiply the semester tuition by two. Later revisions, one-time charges, deposits, hostel and mess costs are separate.

faq.question: Are foreign-national fees the same?
faq.answer: No. The 2026 fee notice separates foreign categories. Standard foreign UG/MTech/MSc/MA tuition is INR 500,000 per semester; ICCR-funded postgraduate SAARC and non-SAARC categories are INR 75,000 and INR 150,000 respectively. Foreign MBA tuition is USD 10,000 per semester. Specific PIO/OCI/OPEN-category exceptions use Indian rates.

faq.question: How do non-campus BS fees and attendance work?
faq.answer: Pay for registered courses/credits each term; no fixed annual residential fee is implied. Data Science, Electronic Systems, Aeronautics and Space Technology and Management and Data Science have their own academic stages, assessment and practical requirements. In-person exams, any required campus laboratory travel and overseas facilitation fees need separate planning.

faq.question: Is accommodation included with every degree?
faq.answer: Residential students use hostel allocations subject to institute arrangements, with hostel and mess charges separate from tuition. Non-campus enrolment does not guarantee accommodation for laboratory visits or examinations. Joint programmes and Cybersecurity field deployments can involve other locations. Accompanying parents need their own accommodation.

faq.question: Are fee remissions and assistantships guaranteed?
faq.answer: Indian tuition exemptions/remissions depend on the specified category and income documents. Eligible Indian MTech HTTA students may receive INR 12,400 per month for up to 22 months with required academic duties; non-HTTA has no such assistantship. International scholarships have separate nomination and award conditions. Admission alone does not guarantee funding.

fee.notes: 2026–27 published semester tuition is INR 100,000; annual baseline INR 200,000 is two-semester arithmetic, not the aggregate admission bill. Later semesters may be revised. One-time charges, deposits, medical/other fees, hostel and mess are additional. Indian SC/ST/PwD students have tuition exemption. Indian General/OBC-NCL/EWS family income below INR 1 lakh has full tuition remission; INR 1–5 lakh has two-thirds remission.

additionalFees.notes: Foreign-national UG tuition INR 500,000 per semester, annualised for two semesters; later revisions possible. Valid PIO/OCI cards issued before 4 March 2021 use maximum Indian fees. Dual degree fee level changes after semester 8.

admissionsContent.overview: B.Tech. Aerospace Engineering is a 4-year IIT Madras award in Chennai. The programme combines disciplinary study with the institute’s academic and practical requirements.

eligibility.intro: These requirements apply to the documented admission route. Qualifications, entrance tests and nationality/category rules must be assessed together.
items: For 2026: Class XII with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, at least five subjects; meet 75% aggregate (65% for eligible SC/ST/PwD) or the category-wise top 20-percentile criterion.
First Class XII appearance normally 2025 or 2026; the specified late 2023–24 board-result exception and compulsory-service relaxation follow the JEE 2026 rules.
Born on/after 1 October 2001; eligible Indian SC/ST/PwD relaxation is five years. The foreign compulsory-military-service exception is assessed separately.
JEE Advanced allows at most two attempts in consecutive years. The earlier IIT-admission exclusion and the stated preparatory/nonreporting/withdrawal exceptions also apply.
Indian and OCI/PIO(I) applicants require the qualifying JEE Main 2026 rank before JEE Advanced. Foreign and OCI/PIO(F) applicants register directly for JEE Advanced without JEE Main.
Qualify JEE Advanced and obtain the programme allocation through JoSAA. Overseas school qualifications need the required equivalence evidence; nationality and OCI/PIO seat categories differ.

evidence.claimText: B.Tech. Aerospace Engineering: normal programme duration 4 years. Regular residential award.

evidence.claimText: For 2026: Class XII with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, at least five subjects; meet 75% aggregate (65% for eligible SC/ST/PwD) or the category-wise top 20-percentile criterion. First Class XII appearance normally 2025 or 2026; the specified late 2023–24 board-result exception and compulsory-service relaxation follow the JEE 2026 rules. Born on/after 1 October 2001; eligible Indian SC/ST/PwD relaxation is five years. The foreign compulsory-military-service exception is assessed separately. JEE Advanced allows at most two attempts in consecutive years. The earlier IIT-admission exclusion and the stated preparatory/nonreporting/withdrawal exceptions also apply. Indian and OCI/PIO(I) applicants require the qualifying JEE Main 2026 rank before JEE Advanced. Foreign and OCI/PIO(F) applicants register directly for JEE Advanced without JEE Main. Qualify JEE Advanced and obtain the programme allocation through JoSAA. Overseas school qualifications need the required equivalence evidence; nationality and OCI/PIO seat categories differ.
evidence.sourceLabel: Exact programme academic and selection requirements

evidence.claimText: Indian Institute of Technology Madras is a public institute in Chennai offering engineering, science, humanities, management and research degrees. Its residential campus supports laboratory and project-based study, while separate non-campus and international interdisciplinary programmes have their own admission and delivery arrangements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Official institution identity and history

evidence.claimText: The wooded Chennai campus brings together academic buildings, laboratories, hostels, sports and student clubs. Gajendra Circle connects the residential, academic and hostel zones. Campus activities include technical and cultural events, student organisations and innovation projects. Non-campus BS learners study through their separate online and examination arrangements rather than receiving a residential campus place.
evidence.sourceLabel: Official campus environment and student activity scope

evidence.claimText: The Chennai campus entrance is on Sardar Patel Road, near Adyar and Velachery, with the address IIT Madras, Chennai 600036. Internal buses connect the gate, Gajendra Circle, academic areas and hostel zones. The campus is distinct from IIT Madras Zanzibar in Tanzania and from partner institutions used by joint programmes. Check the exact reporting or examination location on the offer, particularly for non-campus degrees and joint or field-deployment routes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Official campus address and internal transport

evidence.claimText: Residential engineering master’s programmes combine core and elective courses with project work; approved projects may involve industry or other organisations. Science and engineering curricula include discipline-specific laboratory and computational study. The MBA combines cases, management internship and project work. International interdisciplinary M.Tech programmes add cross-department coursework and a thesis. Cybersecurity includes two years of field deployment after its campus coursework. Electronic Systems and Aeronautics non-campus degrees require specified practical visits; these arrangements differ from full-time campus study.
evidence.sourceLabel: 2026 academic brochure and mode-specific curricula

evidence.claimText: First-year residential undergraduates normally share rooms; later single, double or triple allocations depend on the hostel. Postgraduates use shared or single rooms. Wardens, resident assistant wardens and hostel councils support administration. Hostel and advance mess charges are separate from tuition and require the current notice. Non-campus BS enrolment does not guarantee a hostel place for examinations or laboratory visits; accompanying parents must arrange their own stay.
evidence.sourceLabel: Official room-allocation and hostel administration

evidence.claimText: Residential dining has North Indian/South Indian vegetarian/nonvegetariancuisines; facilities Himalaya/Vindhya/Nilgiris. Specific dietcertificationnotestablished.
